summary: Learning how neural networks turn data into predictions, from a single decision boundary to image models and sequence forecasts.

topics.title: Linear classifiers and gradient descent
topics.description: A decision boundary separates classes using a score calculated from input features. Gradient descent updates its parameters to reduce a measured prediction loss.

topics.title: Backpropagation and dense networks
topics.description: The chain rule carries derivatives backward through a network so its weights can be updated. Dense networks combine several learned layers to classify handwritten digits.

topics.title: Convolution and image features
topics.description: Convolutional filters reuse a small set of weights across an image. Shape-classification exercises connect filters, model size and the effect of rotating the input images.

topics.title: Image regression
topics.description: Clock reading and triangle counting require numerical outputs rather than class labels. The target representation and error measure need to match what the number means, including clock time wrapping around.

topics.title: Segmentation and object detection
topics.description: Segmentation assigns image regions or pixels to a mask, while detection locates objects with labeled boxes. Saved assignments compare prompted masks and a pretrained detector on selected images.

topics.title: Sequence forecasting and baselines
topics.description: Sequence models use earlier observations to predict later ones. Airline and Bitcoin exercises compare learned forecasts with simple reference predictions using chronological test periods.

sourceNote: Spring 2026 saved Assignments 1–9, notebooks, reports and course index.

summary: Working with data in R, comparing groups and fitting statistical models, with attention to uncertainty, assumptions and interpretation.

topics.title: R, data selection and summaries
topics.description: Rows and columns are selected by position or condition, and loops repeat calculations across variables. Means, sample spread and group summaries describe the observations before modeling.

topics.title: ANOVA and group comparisons
topics.description: Analysis of variance compares group means by separating within-group and between-group variation. Pairwise comparisons then ask which differences are supported while accounting for several comparisons.

topics.title: Linear regression
topics.description: A fitted line relates a numerical response to a predictor. Slopes, intercepts, fitted values and residuals connect the model equation with the observed data.

topics.title: Intervals, tests and diagnostics
topics.description: Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests quantify uncertainty under a model. Residual plots help examine whether the assumptions behind those calculations are plausible.

topics.title: Multiple regression and the group final
topics.description: Adding predictors changes each coefficient into a comparison adjusted for the others. The happiness final combines descriptive comparisons with linear and logistic models using the General Social Survey.

sourceNote: Spring 2026 saved Homework 1–7, lecture outline and GSS group-final materials.

summary: Using deterministic equations and stochastic simulations to study biochemical reactions, feedback and variation between repeated runs.

topics.title: Reaction balances and enzyme kinetics
topics.description: Reaction rates determine how species amounts change while conservation relationships connect the variables. Enzyme models lead to the Michaelis–Menten saturation relationship.

topics.title: Competitive inhibition
topics.description: An inhibitor competes for enzyme binding and changes product formation. Comparing inhibited and uninhibited trajectories connects the reaction mechanism with the observed curve.

topics.title: Gene feedback and stable states
topics.description: The lac model connects transport and gene expression through feedback. An equilibrium is a state where the modeled rates balance; stability asks how nearby trajectories behave.

topics.title: Initial conditions and basins of attraction
topics.description: Different starting states can approach different long-term outcomes. A basin map organizes starting conditions according to the stable state they approach.

topics.title: Individual reaction events
topics.description: A stochastic model chooses individual reaction events and waiting times rather than evolving only a smooth average. Repeated runs reveal differences that one deterministic trajectory cannot display.

topics.title: Variability and observation time
topics.description: Product distributions and relative spread summarize repeated simulations. The observation time or chosen time window matters because it determines which product values are being compared.

sourceNote: Fall 2026 tutorial notes and preserved enzyme, lac-feedback, basin and stochastic-comparison exercises.

summary: Building small Python programs from input and arithmetic through control flow, reusable functions, stored data and object-oriented code.

topics.title: Input, arithmetic and decisions
topics.description: Programs convert typed input into values, calculate results and choose a branch according to a condition. Clear input and output connect a small program to the task it performs.

topics.title: Loops and functions
topics.description: Loops repeat a calculation over a range or until a stopping condition is reached. Functions separate reusable calculations from the code that collects input and displays results.

topics.title: Collections and text files
topics.description: Lists, strings and dictionaries organize related values and support lookups. Text-file programs store records between runs and read those records back for display or processing.

topics.title: Classes and inheritance
topics.description: Classes combine an object's data with methods that use or change it. Inheritance shares common fields and behavior while allowing a more specific class to add its own information.

topics.title: SQLite queries
topics.description: A file-based database stores structured records that SQL can sort, filter and summarize. The city exercise uses ordered queries and population aggregates to connect Python with a database.

sourceNote: Summer 2025 original Python chapter assignments, Chapters 2–14, and course index.

summary: Developing Java programs using typed values, control flow, methods, arrays and cooperating classes, then combining them with file input and output.

topics.title: Typed input and control flow
topics.description: Variables have declared types, and input is converted into values before calculation. Conditions, menus and validation loops control which operations a program performs.

topics.title: Methods and arrays
topics.description: Methods name reusable operations with parameters and return values. Arrays store several values of one type, while loops process their entries to calculate totals or select a result.

topics.title: Objects, constructors and composition
topics.description: Classes hold state and expose behavior through methods. Constructors initialize objects, and composition builds a larger object from smaller cooperating objects.

topics.title: Inheritance and abstract classes
topics.description: A subclass extends shared fields or behavior from a parent class. The saved employee and geometry packages include inheritance and abstract geometric-object examples.

topics.title: Files and integrated programs
topics.description: Programs read sample records, calculate results and write structured output. The registration project combines validation, menus, course arrays, tuition calculations and file writing.

sourceNote: Fall 2025 original Java assignments and package folders, including student, employee, geometry and registration programs.

summary: Comparing ways to organize data by the operations they support, their running time and their use of memory.

topics.title: Interfaces and running time
topics.description: An interface specifies what operations a structure supports separately from how they are implemented. Running-time analysis compares how the cost of those operations grows with input size.

topics.title: Array-based lists, stacks and queues
topics.description: Arrays support compact indexed storage, while resizing changes how space is allocated. Stacks, queues and deques expose different rules for adding and removing entries.

topics.title: Linked structures and space efficiency
topics.description: Linked lists connect separate nodes rather than requiring one continuous array. The course compares these representations with structures such as rootish arrays and space-efficient lists.

topics.title: Skiplists and hash tables
topics.description: Skiplists use several linked levels to help search an ordered collection. Hash tables use a computed location to organize lookup, with collision handling when keys share a location.

topics.title: Trees and traversal
topics.description: Tree traversals visit entries in a defined order, and binary search trees use ordering to guide search. The syllabus continues into randomized and balanced search trees and heaps.

topics.title: Later syllabus topics
topics.description: The later outline includes sorting, graphs, tries and B-trees. These are course-outline topics rather than a claim that all later assignments or implementations were completed.

sourceNote: Fall 2026 syllabus topic order and preserved early-course reading and assignment lists; later topics are labeled as syllabus coverage.
